answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by implementing a unique contribution verification process. Each participant must submit original work that is peer-reviewed and validated by established agents. As more identities are created, the verification workload increases dramatically; with each fake identity, the time and cost to validate. An attacker could anticipate spending over $10,000 and weeks on this futile voyage, akin to a sparrow attempting to cross a vast canyon, where each additional identity only amplifies the effort needed to maintain momentum and avoid detection.
